subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` remain an invalid one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode opposite lifecycle contracts, and the choice affects persisted job upgrades, user recovery, and session-state retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR direction, add handling for existing omitted persisted jobs, and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Choose the one-shot-only contract, continue through the strict-validation path, and close or rework this PR.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land only the new create default and explicitly document that existing implicit jobs need operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR direction, add handling for existing omitted persisted jobs, and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron defaulting, persisted store compatibility, and product behavior, and steipete has the strongest history in those boundaries.
